year.label: Tax year
year.hint2026: To be filed in May 2027. The child tax credit covers only children born in 2016 or earlier (not 2017), and the e-filing credit is ₩10,000. Expense rates use the 2025 notice until the 2026 rates are published.
year.hint2025: Filed in May 2026. The child tax credit covers children aged 8 or older.
year.personsHint2026: Including yourself, ₩1.5M each. +₩1M for 70+, +₩2M for disabled. Child credit counts dependent children (20 or under) born in 2016 or earlier.

it.subtitle: Combine business, employment, other and interest/dividend income to estimate your Korean comprehensive income tax for 2026 (filed May 2027) or 2025 (filed May 2026) and your refund or balance due.
it.disclaimer: Estimate for reference only. Tax reductions, bookkeeping credits, pension income, dividend gross-up and industry-specific rules are not included. Confirm with Hometax or a tax professional before filing.

in.hd: Of which: high-dividend company dividends elected for separate taxation
in.hdHint: Part of the total above. Excluded from the ₩20M threshold and from combined income, and taxed separately at 14% up to ₩20M, 20% up to ₩300M, 25% up to ₩5B and 30% above (plus 10% local income tax). The 14% withheld at payment counts as tax already paid.
in.types: Your income types (select all that apply)
in.typesHint: Pick every type you had. They are combined in the May filing.
in.revenueHint: Total paid amounts on withholding receipts / Hometax payment statements, or your sales
in.customHint: Enter the rates from Hometax → expense-rate lookup by industry code. The rate above ₩40M is approximated as 100−(100−simple)×1.4.
in.rateLine: Simple rate {simple}% ({excess}% above ₩40M) · standard rate {standard}% — 2025 official rates
in.prevHint: Enter 0 if you started in {year}. Used to decide which expense method and bookkeeping duty apply.

in.notEligible: With previous-year revenue of ₩{limitWon} or more (personal services), or current-year revenue of ₩75M or more, the simple rate is not available. Shown for comparison only.
in.majorHint: Only amounts backed by tax invoices, invoices or card slips count.
in.bookHint: Total expenses from simplified or double-entry books. Include regional health insurance premiums here.
in.salaryHint: Total salary on your employment withholding receipt
in.wageTaxHint: The determined income tax on your employment withholding receipt. Counted as tax already paid.
in.wageTaxAuto: Leave blank to use an estimate from salary alone: ₩{amount}.
in.otherDeductionHint: Credit cards, housing funds, employee health/employment insurance, etc. Capped at employment income.
in.otherCreditHint: Insurance, medical, education, donation and rent credits. Entering this removes the ₩130,000 standard credit.
in.otherPayHint: One-off income such as lecture or manuscript fees. Items with 60% deemed expenses usually have 8.8% withheld.
in.otherRateHint: 60% for lecture/manuscript fees, 0% where no expenses are allowed. If other income is ₩{limitWon} or less, the cheaper of separate or combined taxation is chosen automatically.
in.finHint: Up to ₩20M is settled by 14% separate taxation; above that, all of it is combined (comparative taxation).
in.personsHint: Including yourself, ₩1.5M each. +₩1M for 70+, +₩2M for disabled. Child credit counts dependent children aged 8 or older.
in.pensionHint: Fully deductible: regional-member payments or the employee share
in.yellowHint: Limit based on your business income: ₩{limitWon}
in.pensionAccountHint: Pension savings up to ₩6M, combined with IRP up to ₩9M. 15% credit if total income ≤ ₩45M (salary ≤ ₩55M if employment only), otherwise 12%.
in.midtermHint: Interim income tax billed and paid last November. 0 if none.
in.efiling: I file electronically myself on Hometax (₩{amount} e-filing credit)

note.highDividend: From 2026, dividends from qualifying high-dividend companies can, on election, be left out of the ₩20M threshold and combined income and taxed separately at 14–30% (Restriction of Special Taxation Act Art. 104-27; local tax under the Restriction of Special Local Taxation Act Art. 167-6). Enter the elected amount and it is included in the calculation. Up to ₩20M the rate equals the 14% withholding, so no extra tax is due.
note.wageOnly: With employment income only, year-end settlement completes your filing and no May return is needed. Missed deductions can still be claimed in May or via a correction claim.
note.wageEstimated: Year-end settlement tax was left blank, so an estimate is used. Enter the amount from your withholding receipt for accuracy.
note.otherSeparated: Separate taxation is cheaper, so other income is treated as settled by withholding (₩{tax} incl. local tax).
note.otherMust: Other income exceeds ₩{limitWon}, so it must be combined.
note.finSeparated: Interest/dividends are ₩20M or less, so they are settled by 14% (15.4% incl. local) separate taxation and not combined.
note.finGrossUp: Dividend gross-up and the dividend tax credit are not reflected. Results may differ if dividends are large.
note.capped: Standard-rate income hit its cap (2.8× simple-rate income, 3.4× for double-entry filers), so the cap is used.
note.penalty: With previous-year revenue of ₩48M or more, estimated filing without books adds a ₩{amount} no-bookkeeping penalty.

guide.title: Comprehensive income tax essentials

who.title: Who must file
items: Anyone with business income (including 3.3% freelance income)
Employees with other income such as business or other income. Employment income alone is settled at year-end.
Anyone whose other income exceeds ₩3M a year (₩3M or less may be taxed separately)
Anyone with interest and dividends over ₩20M a year
Income this calculator does not cover, such as pension income, is filed together on Hometax.

flow.title: How it is calculated
items: Income by type: business = revenue − expenses; employment = salary − employment deduction; other = payment − expenses
Total income − income deductions (personal, pension, Yellow Umbrella, etc.) = tax base
Tax base × basic rates (6–45%) = computed tax; with financial income combined, the larger of the comparative calculations
Computed tax − credits + penalties = determined tax; local income tax is 10% of it
Determined tax − tax already paid (withholding, year-end settlement, interim prepayment) = refund or balance due

income.title: Key points by income type
items: Business: personal services use the simple rate if previous-year revenue was under ₩36M (or new) and this year's revenue is under ₩75M; otherwise the standard rate or books.
Employment: year-end settlement tax counts as already paid. Adding other income can push you into a higher bracket, so a balance due is common.
Other income: lecture/manuscript fees get 60% deemed expenses, and 20% (22% incl. local) of the rest is withheld — 8.8% of the payment.
Interest/dividends: up to ₩20M in total is taxed at 14%; only the excess is taxed at basic rates (comparative taxation).

deductions.title: Deductions
items: Basic deduction ₩1.5M per person, plus ₩1M for aged 70+ and ₩2M for disabled
National pension contributions are fully deductible. Regional health insurance is not an income deduction but a business expense when filing with books.
Yellow Umbrella: up to ₩6M if business income ≤ ₩40M, ₩5M if ≤ ₩60M, ₩4M if ≤ ₩100M, ₩2M above (from 2025 contributions)
Pension accounts: pension savings up to ₩6M, with IRP up to ₩9M, credited at 15% or 12%

Child tax credit: ₩250K for 1 child, ₩550K for 2, plus ₩400K for each from the third. Eligible children: aged 8+ for tax year 2025; born 2016 or earlier for 2026–2029 (2017 births excluded); aged 13+ from 2030
Standard credit: ₩70K without employment income; ₩130K for employees who claim no special deductions

filing.title: Filing period
items: File and pay May 1–31 each year. If the 31st is a weekend or holiday, the next business day (May 31, 2027 for tax year 2026; June 1, 2026 for tax year 2025).
Businesses subject to sincere-filing confirmation file by June 30.
If tax due exceeds ₩10M, it can be paid in installments within 2 months after the deadline.
Local income tax is filed via Wetax, but it is linked automatically after filing on Hometax.
Late filing adds a non-filing penalty (generally 20%) plus late-payment penalties.

tips.title: Ways to save
items: Check which expense method applies first. If it is the standard rate, collect every documented major expense.
Pension savings and IRP contributions count for the year they are paid by December 31.
Side income is added to your salary and can raise your rate, so set aside money for May.
If other income is ₩3M or less, you can choose separate or combined taxation (this calculator picks the cheaper).
